To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the replication of rPIV3 is restricted in the lower respiratory tracts of animals by the insertion of foreign sequence of 3126 nt or more between the HN or L genes and the downstream NCR of the HN, L, or N gene.

rPIV-3s whose genome has been increased in length by more than 3 kilobases by either an additional gene unit or a noncoding region insertion exhibit an unexpected phenotype, that is efficient replication in vitro, but restricted replication in the lower respiratory tracts of animals.

rPIV 3s whose genome has been increased by 3000 nt or more by insertion of a GU or an NC insert exhibit an unexpected host range phenotype: efficient replication in vitro and restricted replication in hamster lungs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of recombinant parainfluenzavirus type 3 (rPV3) as a vector for expression of foreign genes as a multivalent vaccine.
developing recombinant PIV3 (rPI3) viruses as a vector system for expressing foreign genes.
the design of recombinant parainfluenzavirus 3 (r-PIV3) as a vector to deliver foreign antigens for the development of a multivalent vaccine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of insertions of up (to) 3 kb into the PIV3 genome, whether as additional genes or into the NCRs, is to attenuate the resulting virus in the hamster model of infection.
, in the case of PIV3 at least, the effect of insert size on replication in vitro and attenuation in vivo is dependent on whether the insertion is an additional gene or is inserted within a gene.
the length of the inserted sequence has a profound effect on the replication of PIV3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the size of insertions in the genome of a rPIV3 vector is a critical parameter for the replication of the virus in vitro and in animals, and this effect is dependent on the site of insertion in the genome.
the length of the inserted foreign sequence is an important factor in the development of a recombinant PIV3 vector vaccine.
the length of inserted sequence in the PIV3 genome has a major effect on the replication of the virus in vitro and in the lower respiratory tracts of animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in general, it is not a good idea to insert a foreign sequence of more than a few thousand nucleotides into the PIV3 genome.
, when the length of a viral genome is increased by more than about 3000 nt, the virus is restricted in replication in hamsters.
the size of the inserted foreign sequence is a critical parameter in the development of rPIV3 as an effective vaccine.
